title: Lesson 3: BLESS - Listen and Eat - Show Hospitality
description: The second and third BLESS rhythms. Jesus listened and pulled up a chair for you, so you can listen to your one until they feel known and open your table the way God welcomed you.

blocks.text: In Lesson 2 you saw that you are blessed to be a blessing, and you began to pray for your one. The next two rhythms belong together: Listen and Eat. Listening helps someone feel known, and a shared table gives listening room to grow into friendship.

blocks.alt: Jesus sits at a low table with two travelers at Emmaus and breaks a round loaf of bread in his hands

blocks.title: Stay with Us
blocks.text:
On the Sunday Jesus rose, two of His followers walked toward a village called Emmaus, heartbroken. Their hopes had died on a cross. "Jesus himself drew near and went with them. But their eyes were kept from recognizing him" (Luke 24:15-16).

Jesus knew everything that had happened. He had lived it. Yet He asked, "What is this conversation that you are holding with each other as you walk?" and then, "What things?" (Luke 24:17-19), and He let them pour out the whole sad story.

At the village they urged Him, "Stay with us" (Luke 24:29). So the stranger sat down at their table. "He took the bread and blessed and broke it and gave it to them. And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him" (Luke 24:30-31).

The risen Lord asked questions and listened to a story He already knew. Then a simple meal became the place where two friends recognized Him. Listening opened their hearts, and the table opened their eyes.
3.1 - Think of a time someone really listened to you. What did they do that made you feel heard?
Jesus Pulled Up a Chair for You
Before you ever listen to your one or set a place for them, remember who set a place for you. Jesus was famous for the people He ate with, so famous that His critics complained about it.
Now the tax collectors and sinners were all drawing near to hear him. And the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled, saying, "This man receives sinners and eats with them."

You were one of those sinners. Paul says you were once a stranger "having no hope and without God in the world", until Christ brought you near by His blood (Ephesians 2:12-13). Jesus listened to you, welcomed you, and pulled out a chair for you at His table. One day you will sit at His feast, the "marriage supper of the Lamb" (Revelation 19:9). Welcomed people learn to welcome others.
Listen to Your One

Many people go through whole weeks without anyone asking them a real question and waiting for the answer. When you slow down and listen to someone's story, their hopes, their fears, and what they are carrying, you give them a rare gift. Without saying a word, you tell them they matter. People do not care how much you know until they know how much you care.
Know this, my beloved brothers: let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.

Jesus, who had every answer, asked questions anyway. When a blind man named Bartimaeus cried out to Him, Jesus asked, "What do you want me to do for you?" (Mark 10:51). Good listening has that posture: you listen to the person in front of you while quietly asking the Holy Spirit what is really going on and how to love them well.

blocks.title: Ask, Ask Again, Remember
content: Ask. Use open questions that cannot be answered with yes or no. What has your week been like? How did you end up living here? What are you looking forward to?

Ask again. The first answer is usually the surface. Follow it with a second question: What was that like? Tell me more. "The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Proverbs 20:5).
Remember. Write down what you heard, pray about it with your prayer card, and ask about it the next time you see them. Remembering is what turns a conversation into a friendship.

blocks.text: 3.2 - What open question could you ask your one this week?
Eat with Your One

Jesus ate His way through the Gospels. He ate with tax collectors and religious leaders, with fishermen and friends, and even with the man who would betray Him. He was at the table with the wrong people so often that His critics called Him "a friend of tax collectors and sinners" (Luke 7:34). It described His mission.

The Bible's word for hospitality means love of strangers. It reaches past friends, easy people, and people who will invite you back. "Seek to show hospitality" (Romans 12:13). Seeking means you go looking for chances to welcome people instead of waiting until the house is clean.

Hospitality is not the same as entertaining. Entertaining puts the spotlight on your home, your cooking, and you. Hospitality puts it on your guest, so they feel seen, safe, and wanted. The size of your home has nothing to do with the size of your welcome.

blocks.title: The Open Table
content: Hospitality is a seat at your table, your full attention, an unhurried conversation, room for people who are not like you, and a simple meal, even takeout on paper plates, shared gladly.
Hospitality is not a perfect house, a fancy menu, a performance, a sales pitch, or a dinner saved for the friends who will invite you back.

blocks.text: 3.3 - Where has the pressure to impress kept you from opening your home or table more freely?
Pull Up a Chair

Opening your table does not have to start with a dinner party. Invite your one to lunch or coffee. Add one more seat to a meal you were already going to have. Let others host you too. Jesus once invited Himself to dinner at the house of a man nobody wanted to eat with: "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today" (Luke 19:5). Sometimes the best way to open a table is to sit gladly at someone else's.

Then bring the Listen rhythm to the table. Put your phone away. Ask, ask again, and remember. A meal gives a conversation time to go deeper than a wave across the yard ever could. People may say no, and the talk may feel awkward at first, but you do not go alone. The Jesus who drew near on the Emmaus road has promised to be with you always (Matthew 28:20).
3.4 - When will you invite your one to your table, or to coffee, in the next 30 days?
This Week's Practice

Ask your one an open question this week, then ask again. Write down what you hear, and pray about it with your prayer card. Before the month is over, invite your one to a simple meal or a cup of coffee, and listen more than you talk.
Lesson 3 Review

On the road to Emmaus, Jesus listened to two grieving friends, and they recognized Him at the table. He has pulled up a chair for you too, so you are blessed to be a blessing. Listen to your one until they feel known: ask, ask again, and remember. Then open your table, not to impress them but to welcome them, because in Christ, God welcomed you first.
In the next lesson, you will learn the fourth rhythm, Serve, and see how Jesus knelt to wash His disciples' feet.
